limitations: One-at-a-time perturbation of a single parameter group is the weakest form of sensitivity analysis. It cannot detect compensating or interacting misspecification; joint perturbation and full sensitivity functions (Chan & Darwiche style) are required before any deployment claim.
Rank stability under +/-10% is necessary, not sufficient. The structure itself -- which edges exist at all -- dominates parameter uncertainty here.
The +/-10% band is arbitrary and is not an elicited credible interval. Real expert uncertainty on several of these parameters is far wider.

observational_vs_interventional.explanation: 'Bullying_Social_Exclusion' has no parents in this DAG, so no back-door path exists and the mutilated graph equals the original. The two quantities coincide *as a consequence of the assumed structure*, not as a general fact -- in reality schools do not assign this variable at random.

'Child_Labour_Household_Duties' has parents ['Economic_Strain', 'Parent_Availability'], so conditioning on it also carries information back up those edges. do() cuts them, which is why the two quantities differ here.
'Food_Health_Burden' has parents ['Economic_Strain', 'WASH_Quality'], so conditioning on it also carries information back up those edges. do() cuts them, which is why the two quantities differ here.

immutable_intervention_guardrail.refused_with: Refusing to intervene on non-modifiable variable(s) ['Neuro_Type']. do() is restricted to modifiable school/household factors: ['Bullying_Social_Exclusion', 'Child_Labour_Household_Duties', 'Food_Health_Burden', 'Home_Educational_Support', 'School_Accommodation', 'Sensory_Environment', 'Teacher_Resource_Adequacy', 'Transport_Burden', 'WASH_Quality']. Immutable or protected characteristics such as ['Grade_Band', 'Neuro_Type', 'Parent_Education', 'Sector'] are never valid intervention targets.

library_caveat.conclusion: pgmpy.CausalInference.query disagrees with truncated factorisation whenever the conditioning variable lies outside its chosen adjustment set. estimate_intervention_effect therefore computes do() on the mutilated graph and uses pgmpy only as a no-evidence cross-check.

pathway_attenuation_via_attendance.interpretation: A large shift at the first mediator that arrives at the outcome as a small one is attenuation, not absence. If the outcome shift is below the resolution a review team can act on, the model cannot see its own most important modifiable lever and the structure or parameters must change. NOTE: the shift GROWS at Next_Term_Dropout_Risk, which is impossible along a single route. 4 distinct directed paths run from Support_Mismatch to Next_Term_Dropout_Risk in this variant, so signal is arriving outside this chain and transmission_to_outcome is a total across all routes rather than an attenuation factor for this one.
